correctness.rationale: A grid state is a permutation, hence a one-per-row-and-column selection. Equality in the selected-line minimum-sum bound holds exactly when every selected entry is a minimum on that line, which is exactly a perfect matching in the corresponding minimizer graph. Two perfect matchings differ by alternating cycles, and toggling any alternating cycle preserves perfect matching. This proves the trichotomy and the converse identification of Itzlinger loops. The complexity claim follows from Hopcroft--Karp on at most n^2 edges plus linear-time alternating-cycle detection after a matching is known.

originality.rationale: The underlying matching lemmas are classical and are not claimed as new. The inspected 2026 source does not make the minimizer-graph identification and explicitly says its recursive method cannot distinguish several perfect states from none. Targeted published-finding corpus and web searches found no source applying perfect-matching existence plus alternating-cycle uniqueness to close that stated grid-state decision gap.

value.rationale: The source explicitly identifies the inability to separate the no-perfect-state and multiple-perfect-state outcomes as a downside of its procedure. The minimizer-graph reformulation removes that ambiguity exactly, gives an explicit second state whenever nonuniqueness occurs, and supplies a standard polynomial-time implementation path. This is a motivated structural improvement to the computational test used in a current knot Floer/grid-diagram search, rather than an arbitrary rephrasing of a matrix condition.
